messages:
ashley: heads up - alerting just fired for kv-cache memory + batcher tail latency in us-west-2. error rates climbing on several customer routes, paging spiking. seeing continuous-batching pack sizes inflate to ~4x usual.

devops-bot: [Alert] KV_CACHE_MEMORY_HIGH on cluster-prod-us-west-2 (threshold 85%) - triggered at 2025-11-12T02:14:48Z - incident id inc_20251112_021448

mike: confirmed in the dashboard - memory + paging IO correlated with a recent prefetch/prefetch-window tweak rolled 02:00. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cluster-kv/kv-cache?orgId=1&from=169...

jing: what was the change? I thought the packer patch was a harmless perf tweak.

ashley: it was a prefetch expansion and a small packer change to reduce short-request latency by increasing continuous pack window. it looks like that widened window caused packs to merge across long/short mixes. pack sizes jumped and scheduling fairness broke -> short requests are starving on some nodes.

ashley: customer impact: some PLG customers reported 5-10s tail latency and intermittent 504s; enterprise routes with mixed short/long shapes degraded > SLO. CS alerted a small set of customers, waiting on triage.

cs-bot: Notified impacted customers: cust-alpha, cust-gamma. CS ticket created: CS-9876.

oncall-ryan: I'm on it, taking incident. immediate triage plan: 1) pause prefetch and revert packer window on canary nodes 2) reduce packer max_pack_size to 256 temporarily 3) enable per-tenant pack caps and fall back to single-req packs for affected tenants 4) monitor paging and tail latency.

mike: to add - set batcher_throttle for mixed-shape queues to 0.6 so long requests back off.

ashley: steps I'm running now:
```
# rollback prefetch change on canary pool (us-west-2-a)
kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/kv-prefetcher --to-revision=42 --context=prod-us-west-2-a
# patch batcher config to cap pack sizes
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap batcher-config -p '{"data":{"max_pack_size":"256","continuous_window_ms":"40"}}'
# restart batcher on canary
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/batcher-canary-usw2a
```

devops-bot: Deploy queued: batcher-canary-usw2a restart requested by ashley at 2025-11-12T02:20:13Z.

jing: I'm standing by to flip prefetch off cluster-wide if canary shows regression. what's our rollback threshold? 3x error or tail latency >1.5s for 10m?

oncall-ryan: threshold = error >2% or p99 increase > 1.5s sustained for 5m on canary. if hit, roll back to previous packer config and throttle prefetch.

sam: quick note - we should also disable cross-tenant packing on the canary to isolate whether tenant mixing causes starvation. I can patch graft limits now.

ashley: good call. applying cross-tenant packing disable.

ashley: canary metrics after patch (2m): p95 latency down ~200ms, p99 down ~1.1s, memory usage on canary nodes dropped from 92% -> 68%. paging IO reduced ~60%.

mike: that's promising. start gradual rollout to us-west-2-b and -c with the same config. keep packer max_pack_size=256 and continuous_window_ms=40 during rollout.

ashley: rolling to b now, ramp 10% every 3m, will pause on any p99 regression.

devops-bot: [Deploy] batcher-canary-usw2b rolling at 2025-11-12T02:35:12Z (10%).

ashley: cs-bot please update CS-9876 with ETA and mitigation notes (reverted prefetch on canary, rolling configuration patch).

cs-bot: CS-9876 updated - Mitigation: config rollback and pack caps applied to canary, rolling to additional AZs. ETA for full mitigation: 30-45m.

oncall-ryan: ongoing actions:
- monitor pack_size histogram and continuous pack occupancy
- watch per-tenant head-of-line latency for tenant groups A/B/C
- be ready to enable global prefetch throttle flag if paging resurges

mike: follow-up engineering item: we need a safety valve in packer to avoid pack growth beyond a per-tenant bound and to prefer short-request isolation when shapes mixed. filing a follow-up RFC.

ashley: customer note for small PLG customers: temporary increased tail latency possible during rollout. CS to send status update if any new errors appear.

cs-bot: Sent status update to impacted set at 2025-11-12T02:47:30Z.

ashley: after rolling to all AZs (approx 30m), aggregate metrics show p99 back to baseline for most routes, overall cluster mem at 70%, paging normalized. closing on mitigation; will keep incident open for postmortem and action items.

oncall-ryan: nice job team. postmortem scope: root cause analysis of continuous-window tradeoff, scheduler fairness algorithm under mixed shapes, better canary gating for packer changes, and per-tenant pack caps as runtime feature. owner: mike. due EOD tomorrow.

ashley: adding a quick snippet for the hotfix we used so it doesn't get lost:
```
# batcher config hotfix (applied via k8s patch)
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap batcher-config -p '{"data":{"max_pack_size":"256","continuous_window_ms":"40","cross_tenant_packing":"false"}}'
# enable temporary throttle for mixed queue
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' https://control-plane.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags -d '{"flag":"batcher_mixed_queue_throttle","value":0.6}'
```

mike: logging owner for followup items in PM board. assigning postmortem to me.

ashley: I'll keep monitoring for 1h and then handoff to oncall rotation. thanks all. :thumbsup:

oncall-ryan: taking post-handoff watch at 2025-11-12T03:05:50Z.

ashley: incident note: severity S2 - multiple customers impacted but mitigated within 45m, no data loss. will file full postmortem with timeline and mitigations.

devops-bot: Incident inc_20251112_021448 marked mitigated at 2025-11-12T03:00:12Z (mitigation: config rollback + pack caps).
